title: YAPYAP
genre: Co-op horror-comedy / 'friendslop' – online co-op (up to 5–6 players) where wizards cast spells by SPEAKING incantations into the mic, vandalising a procedurally generated tower while avoiding monsters
early_access_date: n/a (full release; free demo from Oct 2025 Steam Next Fest, demo app 3997990)
team_size: ~10, worldwide and remote [CONFIRMED-ish – GameDiscoverCo interview with Ray G.: 'compact ~10 person team is worldwide & remote']; a Chinese-language article says '2–10 people' (vaguer)
developer_background: Studio ~6 years old. Its earlier game BAPBAP went through about 5 pivots before becoming a roguelike PvP free-to-play party game; it did not perform well and Ray said 'we spent way too long' on it. In early 2025, before Peak had shipped, the team deliberately looked for a short-dev (3–6 month) idea and picked 'voice as a mechanic' – a quick, jam-style, 'vibe-first' prototype (hence GameDiscoverCo's 'jammed its way'). No formal public game-jam entry was found. The vandalism mechanic was not in the first-month plan
platforms_and_store_links: Steam: https://store.steampowered.com/app/3834090/YAPYAP/ ; Steam demo: app 3997990 (https://steamdb.info/app/3997990/) ; Windows + macOS only (no console, no Game Pass found)
business_model: Premium $9.99 with launch-period discounts (later -20% / -30% sales); free post-launch content updates; free demo before launch
units_or_downloads: 500,000 copies in ~1 week (announced 2026-02-10) [CONFIRMED – Maison Bap Steam post, via Automaton/Insider Gaming/WN Hub]; 1,000,000 PLAYERS by ~2026-03-18 [CONFIRMED – Steam news post 'YAPYAP – 1M Players!']; >1.15M copies sold (~May 2026), #7 new 2026 release by Steam units [ESTIMATE/reported – GameDiscoverCo, from dev interview + GDCo data]. Current (~Oct 2026): ~1.2–1.3M [ESTIMATE – 10,050 reviews × calibrated ratio ~120–130]. Trackers (all too low, see conflicts): Raijin 440k (Jul 2026) / 494k (latest); PlayTracker ~649k; Gamalytic ~686k; VG Insights ~802k [ESTIMATE – via SteamDB]
peak_concurrent_players: 14,775 all-time Steam peak on 2026-02-08 [ESTIMATE – SteamDB; Automaton cites the same]. SteamCharts average: 4,718 (Feb 2026) → 318 (Aug 2026). Low CCU relative to sales is typical of short-session friend-group co-op
steam_reviews: ~10,050 total, 84% positive, 'Very Positive' (~Sep–Oct 2026) [Raijin]; 9,213 at 84% (Jul 2026, Raijin per brief); ~7,839 (Steambase snapshot); English-only 3,943 at 84%, recent 74% (store snapshot); 2,600 at 81% around 2026-02-10
implied_review_multiplier: Very high: ~190 at week 1 (500k ÷ ~2,600 reviews, 2026-02-10; reviews lag at launch); ~125–150 by May–Jul 2026 (1.15M ÷ ~7.8–9.2k reviews). One of the highest ratios in the dataset – GameDiscoverCo links it to a young, casual audience (only 12% of players aged ≥35 vs 27% average in its Fan Snapshot) who rarely write reviews. Default Boxleiter multipliers (40–60) undercount this game by 2–3x
gross_revenue: 'A bit less than $10M' (~May 2026) [ESTIMATE/reported – GameDiscoverCo]. Spec method: 1.15M × $9.99 × 0.75 ≈ $8.6M (May 2026); ~1.25M × $9.99 × 0.75 ≈ $9.4M (Oct 2026) [ESTIMATE]. Raijin $3.7M (Jul 2026) [ESTIMATE – inconsistent with the confirmed 500k in week 1; discarded]
net_revenue: ≈ $6.1M [ESTIMATE – ~$9.4M gross × (1 − 0.30 Steam cut, under the $10M tier) × 0.93]. Self-published, so all net goes to the studio
production_cost: ≈ $0.35M–$0.75M [ESTIMATE – ~10 remote people × ~12–13 months × $3k–6k/month (mixed worldwide rates); not all may have been full-time]. Studio carried ~6 years of prior costs from BAPBAP. No marketing spend disclosed (largely organic TikTok/Next Fest)
development_time: ~12–13 months: concept chosen early 2025 as a planned 3–6 month 'short-dev' project; demo Oct 2025 (Next Fest); launch 2026-02-03 [ESTIMATE – timeline from GameDiscoverCo]. Overran the 3–6 month plan, partly because buzz arrived before the gameplay was settled
why_popular: Instantly readable, clippable hook: you shout faux-Latin spell names into your mic to cast magic, and mispronunciations, panic and accents become comedy. Co-op friend-group chaos (vandalising a wizard tower, hiding from monsters) fits the 2025–26 'friendslop' wave (Lethal Company, R.E.P.O., Peak). Dark PSX-style horror look juxtaposed with cute, relatable characters. $10 price for multi-packs; young audience; easy to explain to a friend in one sentence
marketing_channels: TikTok first: an early TikTok got ~288k likes before the gameplay loop even existed (buzz-first development) | Free demo in Steam Next Fest Oct 2025: #3 in Valve's Top 10 by unique players among 2,900+ demos | ~900k Steam wishlists at launch [GameDiscoverCo] (Raijin estimates 640–820k) | YouTube/Twitch streamers and clips (voice-casting fails), incl. YouTube video essays on 'friendslop' (Kingfisher) | $9.99 price + launch discount | Steam news posts celebrating milestones (500k, 1M players) amplified by press (Automaton, Insider Gaming, WN Hub) | Discord community
engine: Unity [CONFIRMED – Unity blog 'Games made with Unity: February 2026'; SteamDB demo depots list Unity, FMOD, Mirror + Photon networking, Steamworks]
art_style: Low-poly PSX/retro-3D horror (dark, grainy) with cute, chunky wizard characters
ai_feasibility_justification: AI can: write the voice-command layer (on-device keyword spotting with Vosk/Whisper.cpp or Unity speech plugins; matching a short spell vocabulary is far easier than full speech-to-text), spell/wand logic, a procedural tower generator, destructible props, monster AI and Steam lobby/Mirror/FishNet netcode (Claude Code); generate PSX-style low-poly props and textures (Meshy/Tripo + downscale shaders), character concepts, spell SFX and creepy ambience (ElevenLabs), music (Suno), and faux-Latin spell names. | AI cannot: make voice recognition robust across accents, mic quality and noisy Discord sessions (the #1 player complaint); tune the comedy timing and fear/fun balance; playtest with real friend groups; build the TikTok buzz and Next Fest momentum. Upper end of 4 – becomes 3 if you add heavy physics vandalism sync and multi-language voice support. | Toolset: Claude Code + Unity 6 (Mirror/FishNet + Facepunch Steamworks) or Godot 4 + GodotSteam; Vosk/Whisper.cpp for offline keyword spotting; Meshy/Tripo + PSX shader packs for 3D; ElevenLabs SFX; Suno music; Steam Playtest/Next Fest demo; TikTok devlogs
solo_ai_mvp_cost_time: 5–8 weeks, $250–$700 (Claude Pro/Max, 3D gen sub, PSX asset/shader packs, audio gen, $100 Steam Direct) – 2–4 player Steam-lobby co-op, ~8 voice spells, one procedural tower floor set, 1–2 monsters
solo_ai_polished_cost_time: 4–7 months, $3,000–$10,000 (AI subs ~$100–$300/mo, asset packs, freelance character art/animation polish $1–5k, voice-recognition QA across accents, playtests, trailer, TikTok/streamer outreach, Next Fest demo). Excludes developer's own living costs

data_conflicts: Units: GameDiscoverCo >1.15M copies (~May 2026) vs Raijin 440k (Jul 2026) / 494k (latest) and other trackers at 649k–802k. Resolution: the developer CONFIRMED 500k copies by 2026-02-10, which already exceeds Raijin's July estimate, so Raijin (and probably the other review-driven trackers) undercount. They apply ~45–80x review multipliers, but this young, casual audience reviews far less often (implied ratio ~125–190). GameDiscoverCo's figure (interview with Ray G. plus its own data) is used, and Raijin's $3.7M gross is discarded in favour of 'just under $10M'. '1M players' (dev Steam post, ~2026-03-18) vs '1M copies' (GDCo headline): the dev counted players, not copies. Steam 'players' can include Family Sharing borrowers and refunded copies, so players are likely somewhat above copies. I searched and found NO free weekend, free-to-play period or Game Pass/console release that would inflate the player count, and the free demo is a separate app (3997990), so it is not counted. The 1M-players and 1.15M-copies figures are therefore broadly consistent. Max players: Wikipedia says up to 5, Automaton says up to 6. Review totals differ by snapshot and language filter (store English 3,943 vs all-language ~10k). Wishlists at launch: GDCo ~900k vs Raijin 640–820k
notes: Key lessons: (1) choose a mechanic that is instantly clippable and explainable (speak to cast); (2) the team explicitly chose a small 3–6 month scope after over-investing in a failed F2P game; (3) test the hook on TikTok BEFORE the gameplay is finished – 288k likes on an early clip told them they had something; (4) Next Fest top-3 by players plus ~900k wishlists set up a 500k first week; (5) a cheap price and a young audience mean very high sales-per-review, so do not trust review-based tracker estimates for kid/teen-skewed friendslop. Weakness: depth (buzz arrived before the design was settled) and voice-recognition reliability, which pulled recent reviews down to ~74%
